and tags stay unchanged, and the current filter is kept, matching
delete and order.

The deleteorder command needs its user input parsed into a
DeleteOrderCommand.

Let's add DeleteOrderCommandParser, which works like
DeleteCommandParser and accepts a single positive index. Empty,
zero, negative, non-numeric, overflowing and extra arguments are
all rejected with the command's usage message.

Let's add it to AddressBookParser next to delete, and test that
the command word is dispatched to DeleteOrderCommandParser.

Add fulfilment date, method and notes classes
commitResults.messageBody:
A preorder has items but nothing records when or how the customer
receives it. Task 4 needs a date, a delivery or collection method
and handover notes shared by all items in a preorder.

Let's add FulfilmentDate, FulfilmentMethod and HandoverNotes as
immutable value classes with their own validation and messages.

FulfilmentDate accepts only real calendar dates in YYYY-MM-DD form.
FulfilmentMethod follows ItemStatus and HandoverNotes follows Remark,
so limits and messages stay consistent with item fields.

The date, method and handover notes apply to the whole preorder,
not to each item, so they belong on Preorder.

Let's give Preorder the three details as optional fields, with
getters that return Optional and a withItems method that replaces
the items but keeps the details.

The existing Preorder(List<Item>) constructor stays and leaves all
three details unset, so current callers work unchanged. Item
commands can use withItems to avoid dropping the details when they
rebuild a preorder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save fulfilment details in the data file

Preorder now has a date, method and handover notes, but the data
file does not store them, so they would be lost on restart.

Let's save them as "date", "method" and "handoverNotes" on each
preorder in the JSON file.

A missing or null value loads as unset, so data files from v1.3 and
earlier v1.4 builds still load. An invalid value fails the load with

Let's give FulfilmentDate one display format, such as "20 Dec 2026",
for the card and the summaries to share. It lives in the model so
that model-side summaries can use it without depending on the UI.
Month names are always English, so the display does not change with
the computer's language.

- a collection whose items are all completed

commitResults.messageTitle: Add parsers for preorder fulfilment details
commitResults.messageBody:
The preorder command needs to read a fulfilment date, a method and
handover notes from user input, but there are no prefixes or
parsers for them yet.

Let's add the f/, m/ and h/ prefixes, and parsers for each value.
Dates must be real YYYY-MM-DD dates, methods ignore letter case,
and handover notes are trimmed and limited to one line.

The date and method parsers and their tests match PR #145
exactly, so both PRs can share them without merge conflicts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add preorder command to set fulfilment details
commitResults.messageBody:
A preorder can store a date, a method and handover notes, but there
is no command to set them, so bakers cannot record the delivery or
collection arrangements agreed with a customer.

Let's add "preorder INDEX [f/DATE] [m/METHOD] [h/HANDOVER_NOTES]".
Only the supplied details change, and an empty value clears that
detail, like edititem's empty r/. Items, tags and the postal code
are kept, and a customer without a preorder gets one with no items.

A past date is accepted with a note rather than rejected, so that
late records can still be entered. The success message shows all
three details, because the customer card does not show them yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the preorder command in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The preorder command is not in the User Guide, so bakers cannot
find its format, the rule that an empty value clears a detail, or
what the past-date note means.

Let's add a preorder section next to track and deleteorder with a
prefix table, examples based on the sample data, and the exact
success and error messages. Let's also add preorder to the command
summary and to the commands that keep the current search.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add sort command to order by date
commitResults.messageBody:
During busy seasons, the baker needs to see which preorders are
handed over first. The customer list can only be shown in saved order
or grouped by postal code.

Let's add a SortCommand that orders the displayed customers by the
handover date of their preorder, earliest first. Customers with no
preorder or no date are listed last, and equal dates are ordered by
name ignoring case. The current find filter is kept, like group
postal.

SortCommand exists, but the app does not recognise the sort command
word, so users cannot run it.

Let's add a SortCommandParser and register it in AddressBookParser.
It accepts "date" ignoring case and surrounding spaces, so a fast
typist's "sort DATE" still works. Any other or extra argument shows
the usage message, so users learn the one supported sort key.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the sort command in the UG
Call the sort key the fulfilment date
commitResults.messageBody:
The sort command and its UG section call the date a "handover date",
but the preorder command and the model call it the fulfilment date,
and "handover" also names the handover notes. Users could think the
command sorts by notes. The UG also does not say how a date is set.

Let's use "fulfilment date" in the messages and the UG, and link the
sort section to the preorder command that sets the date. Also move
the command summary row next to Untag, so it does not sit beside the
Find row that several open PRs change.

commitResults.messageBody:
Loading a v1.3 data file turns each preorder into one item without a
quantity. Logging the conversion makes it easier to tell why an item
shows "quantity needed".

commitResults.messageBody:

preorder. The preorder class diagram, the saved JSON example and the
v1.3 loading notes now include them, and a new design consideration
explains why they belong to the preorder rather than to each item.

Also use "quantity needed" in lower case, as the card now shares that
text with the edititem message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restyle the window and customer cards in brown
commitResults.messageBody:
The window kept AB3's grey theme, and each contact detail took its own
line on the card, so few customers fit on screen. The result box was
also fixed at 100 px, so longer usage messages were cut off or scrolled
sideways.

The window now uses a warm brown theme with two bundled OFL fonts. Each
card shows its number on the left, the name with tags, phone and email
on one line, and the address with the postal code. Item numbers get
their own column, a missing quantity or postal code gets a warning
icon, and COMPLETED gets a tick. Matching items keep a yellow box. The
result box wraps and grows to fit the whole message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the summaries and help in a side panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The delivery preparation summary sat above the customer list, so at
the default window size only about one card fit under it, and the
product preparation summary stacked on top of it during a product
search. Help opened a separate window that had to be closed with the
mouse.

The window now has two columns. The command box, results and customer
list are on the left, and a side panel on the right shows one view at
a time: help after the help command, the product summary during a
product search, and the delivery summary otherwise. Help stays until
the next successful command.

The left column keeps at least 450 px, so cards still wrap whole
words, and the panel at least 300 px. The window's minimum width is
800 px to fit both, and the default width is now 1000 px.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tighten the gaps around the customer list in a narrow window
commitResults.messageBody:
At the window's minimum width, the left column is only about 470 px,
and the gaps around the list and inside each card left little room
for the cards' text.

Below 900 px, the window gets a compact style class that shrinks
those gaps, which gives the cards about 40 px more width. The paddings
that change are now in DarkTheme.css instead of the FXML files, so the
class can switch them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the UG and DG for the brown card
commitResults.messageBody:
Describe the new card layout in the UG, and use the card's shorter
"Qty needed" wording where the guides quote it. Also replace the UG's
screenshot, which still showed the v1.3 mockup.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the UG and DG for the side panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG described help as a separate window and placed both summaries
above the customer list. It now says they share the side panel, with a
new screenshot of help in the panel. The DG describes the two columns
and the compact layout, and its UI diagram shows SidePanel and its
three views instead of HelpWindow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Switch the compact layout with a pseudo-class
commitResults.messageBody:
A compact window is either on or off, which is what JavaFX
pseudo-classes are for. pseudoClassStateChanged replaces the code that
added or removed a style class, so there are no branches left to get
out of step.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the help panel's Copy URL button
Credit AB3, the libraries and the fonts in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG's Acknowledgements section was still AB3's placeholder, and
the course requires it to credit everything reused. It now credits
AB3, the three libraries and the two bundled fonts, which the product
website also lists. Also add a picture of a card to the UG's card
description.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bring the UG and DG in line with the side panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG still listed the help window's minimize problem as a known
issue, and its command summary had no exit row. Add the two FAQ
entries the course suggests, for double-clicking the JAR and for
write-protected folders.

In the DG, the launch test now starts LeBake from a terminal, as the
UG says, and checks the smallest window. A new manual test walks
through the side panel's three views.
Wrap long customer addresses in cards

The usage message listed five matching rules that the user guide
already explains. At the minimum window width it took 12 lines, so the
result box left little room for the customer list. It now shows only
the parameters and an example, in 7 lines.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use the system font instead of bundled fonts
commitResults.messageBody:
The course requires approval for third-party libraries but says
nothing about fonts, and the team preferred not to bundle them without
that confirmation. The theme now uses Segoe UI, as AB3 does, and falls
back to the system font where it is missing. The fonts, their licences
and their acknowledgements are removed, and the UG images are updated.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit the window on a 1280x720 screen at 150%
commitResults.messageBody:
That screen is 480 px tall at 150%, and 432 px above the Windows 11
taskbar, but the window could not be shorter than 600 px.

Lower the minimum height to 420 px. The customer list now keeps at
least 80 px, enough for a card's index and name, and a long message in
the result box scrolls when the window is too short for both. The
window also opens no larger than the screen.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove tag editing from the edit command
commitResults.messageBody:
Limit edit to name, phone, email and address while preserving existing
customer tags. Treat t/ as ordinary text, consistent with other
unrecognized prefixes.

Update affected tests and helpers for the supported edit fields.

Remove the tag-specific preamble test because edit treats all
unrecognized prefixes the same way. Keep generic coverage for invalid
preambles and literal prefix-like address text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update user guide for supported edit fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Remove tag editing from edit syntax, examples and the command summary.
Clarify that an edit requires a supported field and preserves omitted
fields and existing tags.

Customer name validation accepts digits but rejects apostrophes and
hyphens. Names created outside the command parser retain extra spaces.

Allow letters, spaces, apostrophes and hyphens, reject blank names
and digits, and normalize spaces while preserving capitalization.
Apply these rules consistently through Name and update validation
and regression tests.

Refs AY2627S1-CS2103T-F09-3/tp#57

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore case when checking duplicate customers
commitResults.messageBody:
Duplicate checks treat capitalization changes as distinct names,
allowing customers with equivalent normalized names to coexist.

Compare normalized customer names without regard to case. Add model
coverage for duplicate rejection, retaining a customer's own name,
and preserving data after rejected updates. Keep ordinary equality
case-sensitive so display capitalization edits remain detectable.

Refs AY2627S1-CS2103T-F09-3/tp#57

commitResults.messageTitle: Test customer name rules in add and edit commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Command tests do not cover punctuation and spacing normalization or
duplicate names that differ in capitalization and spacing.

Add parser and command coverage for valid and invalid names,
duplicates hidden by filtering, and edits that retain a customer's
own name. Verify display capitalization and unchanged data after
rejected commands, using a shared name fixture with punctuation.

Refs AY2627S1-CS2103T-F09-3/tp#57

commitResults.messageTitle: Test and document stored customer name rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage tests lack coverage for normalized names and duplicates
that differ only in capitalization and spacing. The user guide
does not explain these rules or their effect on saved data.

Add JSON fixtures and storage tests for valid punctuation,
normalization, invalid names, duplicate rejection, and saving and
reloading names while preserving capitalization. Document the
add and edit rules and compatibility with older data files.

Refs AY2627S1-CS2103T-F09-3/tp#57

commitResults.messageBody:
Name validation accepts Unicode letters and punctuation-only values.
Require at least one English letter and limit names to A-Z and a-z,

Update the model tests and normalization fixtures to match this rule.

commitResults.messageBody:

Verify that add and edit parsing, shared name parsing and JSON loading
reject these inputs with the name constraint message.

The user guide describes general letters as valid and lists an
accented name as a valid example.

commitResults.messageBody:
TrackCommand supports filtering, but users cannot invoke it through

Parse optional status arguments, reject malformed input, and route
track commands through AddressBookParser. Cover parsing and routing
with tests.

Track command tests cover parsing and filtering in isolation.

Add command workflows to verify filter replacement, list restoration,
invalid input, and deletion using displayed indexes. Check that status
changes update filtered views without rerunning track.
Implement track command

Customer searching is tied to a name-only predicate, which leaves no
shared structure for combining the upcoming v1.4 search fields.

Introduce immutable AND criteria with independent text and tag matchers.
Document the extension contract, including same-item matching, and cover
the foundation with unit and model integration tests.

Find accepts only bare name keywords, so users cannot narrow customer
results using contact details or tags.

Require explicit prefixes for name, phone, email, address and tag searches.
Combine supplied criteria using AND and reject blank, repeated or
unsupported fields without replacing the previous results.

Update parser and command coverage, integration tests and user/developer
guidance for the prefix-only syntax.

TagCriterion.toString() lacks test coverage, leaving one changed line
uncovered in the PR coverage report.

Verify the formatted tag representation to cover the missing line and
protect the diagnostic output.

Search criteria are applied only as list predicates, leaving no shared
state for commands or a future criteria display to observe.

Store immutable active criteria and bind the filtered list to them.
Expose read-only observation through Model and Logic, retain existing
track matching, and cover replacement, reset and failure behavior.

Validation: all 512 tests and Checkstyle pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve search criteria after customer changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding or editing a customer clears the active search and restores every
customer, interrupting filtered workflows.

Preserve criteria during customer updates and let the observable list
refresh matching results. Cover additions, edits, tag and preorder
changes, and displayed indexes; document the search lifecycle.

Validation: 518 tests pass; main and test Checkstyle report no errors.

Refs: #117

Resolve status imports for the item model and retain prefixed searches

commitResults.messageBody:
Search updates have no model-level diagnostics, making applied filters
and their result counts harder to trace.

Log criteria application and reset through LogsCenter, including a

The find parser rejects empty searches, but direct FindCommand
construction accepts them and can reset the filter to all customers.

Require at least one criterion in the constructor after the null check,
and cover rejection with a focused test. Keep empty criteria valid in
the model so list can reset the search.

Validation: ./gradlew check coverage passes with 616 tests and no
Checkstyle violations.

Master replaces PreorderStatusPredicate with ItemCriterion, leaving the
search logging tests incompatible with the updated search workflow.

Merge master and align the tests with ItemCriterion. Add
SearchCriteria.isEmpty() to express the find guard and reset check
directly without depending on the model's show-all constant.

Validation: 811 tests pass with no Checkstyle violations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into active criteria display
commitResults.messageBody:
Bring the display branch up to date with the current search model and
delivery summary. Preserve both UI panels and migrate status-only badges
to ItemCriterion without restoring the deleted status predicate.

Handle the new handover-notes text field and retain the existing matching
behavior. Postal, product, date and method badge formats remain follow-up
work.

Validation: ./gradlew check coverage reports 894 passing tests and no
Checkstyle violations. The existing method-search UI test still logs an
unsupported criterion until method formatting is added.

Postal searches use a criterion that the active-filter formatter does
not support, leaving postal filters without a readable badge.

Expose the immutable search digits and display them in a Postal badge,
preserving leading zeros and the full query. Keep postal badges after

Cover formatting, stable ordering, unchanged results, rejected queries,
customer updates, filter resets and command-box focus.

Validation: 76 focused tests pass, Checkstyle reports no violations, and
the targeted Javadoc check passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Display combined product and status criteria
commitResults.messageBody:
Product searches use ItemCriterion, but the display only formats its
status-only form. Keep the product and accepted statuses together in one
badge to reflect matching conditions on the same item.

Show Any status for product-only searches, including completed items, and
retain the existing status-only and tracking labels. Preserve complete
values and significant spacing, and document the formats.

Cover same-item matching, customer combinations, item updates, tracking,
invalid queries, filter resets, focus and long wrapping product values.

Validation: 124 focused tests, Checkstyle and targeted Javadocs pass.

Date and method searches use criteria that the badge formatter does not
yet support, leaving their active filters undisplayed.

Expose the immutable matching values and add readable Date and Method
badges. Reuse the existing English date format and keep a stable order
alongside handover notes and the other criteria.

Cover all eleven find prefixes together, empty preorders, rejected
queries, preorder changes, wrapping and focus. Fail badge UI tests on
uncaught JavaFX callback errors, and update the guides.

Validation: ./gradlew check coverage passes with 907 tests and no
Checkstyle violations or uncaught UI errors. Targeted Javadocs pass.
